```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tinyAM)
study_report <- Sys.getenv("TINYAM_PLD_STUDY_REPORT", unset =
  "https://github.com/PaulRegular/tinyAM/blob/main/analysis/formula_expansion/pld_validation_report.Rmd")
guide_root <- Sys.getenv("TINYAM_GUIDE_ROOT")
source_files <- if (nzchar(guide_root)) {
  c(list.files(file.path(guide_root, "R"), "[.]R$", full.names = TRUE),
    file.path(guide_root, "NAMESPACE"))
} else {
  list.files(system.file("R", package = "tinyAM"), full.names = TRUE)
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  cache.extra = list(R = getRversion(), RTMB = packageVersion("RTMB"),
    sources = unname(tools::md5sum(source_files)), inputs = cod_obs))
```

Northern cod catch-at-age estimates and the autumn survey recorded zeros at
some ages. A model can use those observations to learn about low predicted
catches or indices. This example uses the NCAM-inspired model from the
[comparison guide](compare-assessments.html) to ask how fitting sampled zeros
changes the estimated stock history.

## Identify sampled zeros

Pool ages 14–20 into a single 14+ observation for each catch and survey year.
The total is zero only if all seven ages were sampled and every value was zero.
If any constituent age is missing, the total is missing. Keep older catch
rows with missing observations to retain the required input grid and keep
weights and maturity through age 20 for the biomass calculations.

```{r inputs}
dat <- cod_obs
pool_older <- function(data) {
  older <- subset(data, age %in% 14:20)
  by_year <- split(older, older$year)
  totals <- vapply(by_year, function(d) {
    if (setequal(d$age, 14:20)) sum(d$obs) else NA_real_
  }, numeric(1))
  terminal <- data$age == 14
  data$obs[terminal] <- totals[as.character(data$year[terminal])]
  data$obs[data$age > 14] <- NA_real_
  data
}
dat$catch <- pool_older(dat$catch)
dat$index <- subset(pool_older(dat$index), age <= 14)

counts <- function(data) {
  y <- subset(data, year %in% 1983:2025 & age %in% 2:14)$obs
  c(Positive = sum(y > 0, na.rm = TRUE), Zero = sum(y == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    Missing = sum(is.na(y)))
}
rbind(Catch = counts(dat$catch), Survey = counts(dat$index))
```

## Compare observation families

Fit the NCAM-inspired structure with lognormal observations, then change
both the catch and the Fall 2J3KL survey to Poisson-link delta lognormal
(PLD). This family uses the predicted catch or index to determine both the
chance of a zero and the size of positive observations. Its prediction
represents the mean over zeros and positives. The lognormal family fits
positive observations and reports their median. See the
[observation family equations](../reference/observation_families.html).

```{r fits, cache=TRUE, results="hide"}
ncam <- fit_tam(dat, years = 1983:2025, ages = 2:14,
  N_settings = list(process = "off", init = "exp"),
  rec_settings = list(process = "rw"),
  F_settings = list(process = "ar1", mu_form = ~ 1, mean_ages = 5:14),
  M_settings = list(process = "ar1", mu_supplied = ~ I(0.3),
    age_breaks = c(2, 5, 8, 14), mean_ages = 5:14),
  catch_settings = list(sd_form = ~ 1),
  index_settings = list(sd_form = ~ 1, q_form = ~ mono(q_block)),
  silent = TRUE
)

ncam_pld <- update(ncam,
  catch_settings = list(family = pld_lognormal()),
  index_settings = list(family = pld_lognormal())
)
```

```{r checks}
check_tam(Lognormal = ncam, PLD = ncam_pld)
subset(tidy_par(ncam_pld)$fixed, par %in% c("y50_catch", "y50_index"),
  select = c(par, coef, est, lwr, upr, unit))
```

`y50_catch` and `y50_index` are the predicted catch and survey index with an
even chance of a sampled zero. Each has its own fitted value. For catches,
the model describes zeros in reported numbers at age, including zeros from
limited age sampling. A reported zero alone cannot establish that no fish of
that age were removed.

## Check the zeros and positive observations

In the plots below, points show observed zero frequencies and the line shows
average fitted zero probabilities for the same years. The residual plots use
the fitted distribution of zeros and positive values. Hover over a point to
inspect its residual or switch to Standardized to examine the positive
observations alone.

```{r diagnostic-functions}
d <- tidy_obs_pred(ncam_pld)
plot_zero_frequency <- function(data) {
  sampled <- subset(data, is_observed & !is_structural)
  sampled$zero <- as.numeric(sampled$obs == 0)
  frequency <- aggregate(cbind(obs = zero, pred = p_zero) ~ age, sampled, mean)
  plot_obs_pred(frequency, x = ~age, xlab = "Age", color = I(tam_cols()[1]),
    ylab = "Zero frequency", add_buttons = FALSE) |>
    plotly::layout(yaxis = list(range = c(0, 1)))
}
```

### Catch

```{r catch-diagnostics}
plot_zero_frequency(d$catch)
plot_resid(d$catch, x = ~age, xlab = "Age")
```

### Autumn survey

```{r survey-diagnostics}
plot_zero_frequency(d$index)
plot_resid(d$index, x = ~age, xlab = "Age")
```

Patterns by age or year can reveal shortcomings in the one-scale detection
model. These residuals condition on the fitted population, so they describe
agreement with the data used to fit it.

## See what changes in the assessment

```{r trajectories}
recruitment <- get_recruitment(Lognormal = ncam, PLD = ncam_pld)
ssb <- get_ssb(Lognormal = ncam, PLD = ncam_pld)
cols <- tam_pal(2)
plot_trend(recruitment, color = ~model, colors = cols,
  ylab = "Recruitment (thousand fish)")
plot_trend(ssb, color = ~model, colors = cols,
  ylab = "Spawning biomass (tonnes)")
```

Both fits pass numerical checks. The PLD fit estimates 788,000 tonnes of
spawning biomass in 2025, about 9% higher than the lognormal fit. The fitted
survey expected about 73 zeros across the series and observed 72. The fit
expected about 49 catch zeros and observed 57. Use the age plots to see
which catches contribute to that difference.

```{r dashboard, eval=FALSE}
vis_tam(Lognormal = ncam, PLD = ncam_pld)
```

This stock comparison measures sensitivity to the observation assumption.
The simulation study compares the estimated stock histories with known
population trajectories. Check the stock trajectories alongside the
numerical diagnostics and zero calibration.
[Simulation study](`r study_report`)
